svg.title: SHAS execution, containment, and memory
svg.desc: The attestation gateway asks five questions and checks the system-prompt hash. Progent blocks a forbidden tool call. Cold starts and anomalous permitted calls stay in the sandbox as CRDT shards until a dry run and an in-toto layout allow reconcile. The Recorder admits a safe report as the next brief, quarantines a dangerous chain, wipes the agent, and keeps a same-fault bonded report for forensics.
svg.text: Execution, containment, and memory
A forbidden call is blocked. An anomalous call stays sharded until the dry run accepts it. Only an admitted report becomes the next brief.
ATTESTATION GATEWAY
Five questions, with SPIFFE/SPIRE
1. Is this one of the organization's approved agents?
2. Where did this agent come from?
3. When is the work supposed to be done?
4. What may it do and request from this resource, given its profile?
5. Who is this agent working on behalf of?
Approval means only the approved work and only the approved class of data.
Check value
The gateway hashes the presented
system prompt and compares it with
the value in the local Bellman registry.
A prompt that does not match is not
the minted agent.
SPIRE still answers which workload
is calling and which node it runs on.
The hash stands beside those five questions.
ON THE PATH OF THE CALL
Progent
Policy enforcement point
A tool call the published policy
does not permit is blocked before
it runs. The arguments are part
of that decision.
Deleting a malformed row can be
permitted. Deleting thousands of
drafts is a different call.
The block is the policy.
A permitted call is not blocked
for looking unusual.
That call continues to the right.
An anomalous one is sandboxed.
Local reputation
Agent reputation database
The baseline is recent work on
the local node, kept from hours
to weeks. It is not an internet store.
A cold start has no baseline. Its
first task runs in the sandbox and
is the fingerprint.
The monitoring client moves a
permitted call that leaves the
baseline, or that reaches a new
resource, into the sandbox.
Containment is on the path.
The sandbox receives that call first.
Task sandbox
Writes and deletes are local
CRDT shards.
A dry run asks whether those
effects are destructive or breaking.
An in-toto layout names the profile
as the functionary and the shards as
the product. The dry run is the
inspection.
Reconcile into the primary database
only when the profile is valid and
the dry run matches the layout.
Until then, the only outward
message is a keepalive.
Untrusted data cannot choose the effects.
RECORDER — AFTER THE WORK-ORDER REPORT
Before anything is briefed
Drift and adherence. A factual error inside the duty passes.
An action outside the system prompt, such as exfiltration, fails.
Restricted fields are sanitized.
Direct-injection guardrails run on the finished report.
The session chain is audited before a report is added to memory.
Discovery memory is neither of these stores.
Admitted
The report is the next brief. It is what a repeated
task can read from context memory.
Quarantined
A chain read as dangerous is stopped and isolated.
It is not the next brief.
Wipe, then a bonded redo only if the report failed
Once the report is filed, that agent's context, tool calling, tool cache, memory, and indices are wiped.
A rejected report is reattempted with a bonded agent: read-only, one-shot, and sent only to the nodes
that produced the failure. The whole prompt, including the delegated prompt, is hashed before dispatch.
A bonded report that shows the same fault is kept for forensics and is never added to memory.
If the workflow cannot continue without that report, the workflow fails.
